Bringing 
India Closer to Joy
Joy is a craving answered. The missing 
ingredient at the right time. A last-minute table for dinner. A quick bite between meetings. A thoughtful gift across the city. A task handled before the day gets away.
Swiggy shortens the distance between wanting and having, planning and 
experiencing, desire and delight.Our platform now powers many missions, creating millions of moments that bring India closer:Technology helps us understand what each moment needs. Our network helps us respond with speed, choice, affordability and reliability. This allows us to serve more occasions, make convenience feel effortless and bring joy within reach.Joy should travel beyond the order. Its impact should be felt in more livelihoods, greater inclusion, thriving communities and a lighter footprint on the planet. As our role in everyday life deepens, we remain focused on improving safety and well-being, reducing waste and emissions and building responsibly.
Closer to the food 
people love.
Closer to products that 
make daily life easier.
Closer to experiences 
worth sharing.
Closer to opportunities 
for every partner.
Not every expression of joy has to be grand.
Sometimes, it is simply about having the right thing within reach.
More needs met. More moments made. 
More reasons for joy.

About Swiggy
Delivering 
Convenience that Keeps Pace with India
From midnight hunger pangs and office lunches to festive 
orders and forgotten essentials, we power millions of everyday decisions through a platform designed to make convenience faster, simpler, smarter and effortless. 
Swiggy has grown into one of India’s leading 
convenience platforms, serving the changing needs of urban consumers. Through a unified app and integrated ecosystem, we bring together food delivery, quick commerce, dining out, events and emerging hyperlocal services into one seamless experience.
What makes our platform distinctive is not just 
the breadth of services, but how they work together. A shared technology backbone, fulfilment network, membership ecosystem and partner base enable us to serve multiple everyday use cases while continuously improving speed, selection, affordability and reliability. As consumer expectations evolve, we continue to expand the role we play in everyday life through customer-backward innovation, deeper personalisation and high-frequency engagement across categories.
At the same time, we remain focussed on 
building responsibly. Across our platform, we continue to strengthen initiatives around delivery partner welfare, sustainability, governance, responsible sourcing and community impact, while building a business designed for long-term resilience and inclusive growth.Mission
Elevate the quality 
of life of urban consumers by offering unparalleled convenience

Our Strengths
Why Swiggy Wins
Swiggy’s advantage lies in how many things come together  
at once. A trusted brand. A scaled technology backbone.  A wide partner network. Deep consumer understanding. Strong execution. Together, these strengths help us spot emerging needs early, build for them quickly and scale them across India with speed and discipline.
Pioneer in 
Hyperlocal Commerce with Strong Brand Equity
We helped shape India’s hyperlocal commerce 
story. From Food Delivery to Quick Commerce, Swiggy has become a trusted, category-defining brand built on speed, reliability and everyday relevance.
Scalable, Modular 
Tech Stack
Our technology is built to move fast. A reusable, 
modular stack helps us launch, test and scale new propositions efficiently across businesses, while improving reliability, personalisation and operating leverage.Growing and 
Highly Engaged User Base
More users are choosing Swiggy. More often. 
As we expand use cases across food, grocery, dining, events and more, we continue to deepen engagement and increase platform stickiness.
Powerful Network 
Effects
Every side of the platform strengthens the other. 
More users attract more partners. More partners improve selection. Better selection drives convenience, repeat behaviour and stronger value creation across the ecosystem.Preferred Platform 
for Partners
We help partners grow. Through discovery, 
fulfilment, analytics, advertising and customer access, Swiggy enables restaurants, merchants and brands to reach more users and build stronger businesses.
Proven Leadership 
and Governance
Our leadership brings founder-led ambition, 
operational depth and public-market discipline. Strong governance, responsible growth and disciplined execution guide how we scale for the long term.Innovation-Driven 
Culture
We keep asking what can be made faster, 
simpler or more useful. This mindset powers new offerings, sharper propositions and constant experimentation that help us stay close to evolving consumer needs.
Serving Many 
Missions
From vegetables and milk to cakes, toys, make-
up, phone chargers, small appliances, restaurant bookings and more, Swiggy is built to serve a wide range of everyday missions. This breadth helps us stay relevant across more moments, needs and occasions in a consumer’s life.

Chairman’s Message
Building for India’s 
Next Consumption Era
Dear Shareholders,
It gives me great pleasure to write to 
you at an important stage in Swiggy’s journey. FY 2025-26 was our first full year as a listed company. It marked the beginning of a more mature chapter, where scale, ambition and innovation were matched by stronger discipline, greater transparency and a deeper focus on long-term value creation. The progress achieved during the year reaffirms the strength of your Company’s business model and the clarity of its strategy.
India entered the year on a strong 
economic footing. Despite global uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and uneven growth across major economies, the Indian economy continued to show resilience. Growth was supported by domestic consumption, expanding services activity, infrastructure investment, easing inflation and improving real incomes. Household consumption remained central to India’s growth story, with private final consumption expenditure accounting for its highest share of GDP in over a decade.This backdrop is significant for 
Swiggy. Your Company operates at the intersection of consumption, technology and logistics. As India’s digital economy expands, consumers are becoming more comfortable with app-led commerce, and convenience is moving from being a premium proposition to an everyday expectation. India’s retail market remains digitally underpenetrated. Quick commerce is still early in its evolution. Food delivery continues to have meaningful headroom as more consumers and meal occasions move online. Dining out, events, household essentials, personal care and other everyday needs are all being reshaped by digital access, reliable fulfilment and wider choice.
Swiggy was built for this shift. Over 
the years, your Company has not merely participated in emerging categories; it has helped create and shape them. From food delivery to quick commerce, from dining out to newer convenience-led services, Swiggy has designed solutions around real, everyday consumer needs. The purpose has remained simple yet powerful: to elevate the quality of life of urban consumers by offering unparalleled convenience.
During the year, this purpose 
translated into broad-based progress across the platform. Food Delivery continued to deepen engagement by expanding the range of occasions and consumer needs it serves. Quick Commerce scaled in a large and competitive market, while strengthening its proposition as a broader everyday convenience platform. Out-of-Home Consumption delivered its first full year of profitability, showing how adjacent businesses can become meaningful contributors when integrated well. Across the platform, increasing cross-pollination continued to reinforce the strength of Swiggy’s integrated
 ecosy
stem.The Board recognises that leadership in fast-growing sectors requires staying power, financial prudence, robust governance and consumer confidence. This philosophy guided our approach to capital deployment. During the year, Swiggy strengthened its balance sheet through the successful Qualified Institutional Placement of INR 10,000 Crores. Along with the monetisation of the Rapido investment, this timely infusion gives your Company the strategic flexibility to invest for the future, navigate competitive intensity and pursue long-term value creation  
with confidence.
Technology and innovation hav e 
alw
ays been fundamental to Swiggy’s 
culture. They allow us to solve 
evolving consumer needs, improve partner experience and make convenience more reliable, accessible and scalable. What gives the Board confidence is not experimentation alone, but the quality of execution, learning and accountability behind it. As Swiggy grows, this balance between ambition and rigour will remain critical.
Responsible growth is equally 
central to the Company’s future. NSE Sustainability Ratings & Analytics has placed the Company in the ‘Leader’ category, reflecting Swiggy’s performance across environment, social and governance parameters. The Company also continues to advance its 2030 Sustainability Goals, anchored in Climate, Community and Conscience. These include commitments such as achieving a 100% EV delivery fleet, transitioning to 100% renewable energy in direct operations, strengthening circular packaging practices, upskilling and engaging 1 million individuals in the value chain, empowering 100,000 women across the ecosystem, improving delivery partner welfare and strengthening governance and data
 privacy.Gov
ernance remains a key priority 
for the Board. The transition to public markets has strengthened Swiggy’s commitment to transparency, disclosure quality, independent oversight and stakeholder engagement. Our aim is to build a company that not only meets the expectations of a listed enterprise, but earns confidence consistently as an institution operating at the centre of India’s evolving digital consumption
 economy.
A
s Swiggy enters its next phase, our 
priorities are clear: prudent capital allocation, continued technology investments, sharper differentiation and steady progress towards profitability. The journey so far has been exciting, but the future offers an even larger canvas. We will use the foundation built over the years, and the lessons learned along the way, to strengthen our businesses, deepen customer understanding, maintain cost discipline and create sustainable value.
On behalf of the Board, I thank our 
shareholders for their continued confidence in Swiggy. I also acknowledge the dedication of the management team and employees, and the trust of our customers, delivery partners, restaurant partners, merchant partners and brand partners, whose collective contribution continues to strengthen the Company’s platform and purpose.
Swiggy’s next chapter will be shaped 
by the same conviction that has brought us here: to keep building with purpose, serving with care and creating an institution worthy of India’s next consumption era.
Warm regards,Anand Kripalu
ChairpersonSwiggy Limited

MD & Group CEO’s Message
Building with  
Speed, Discipline and ConvictionDear Shareholders,
FY 2025-26 was a year in which 
we challenged the conventional narrative for a newly listed company. We increased our innovation quotient, strengthened execution across businesses and focussed on building the key blocks of our growth trajectory. At Swiggy, the year reinforced a belief that has shaped us from the beginning: consumer-backward innovation and capital-efficient execution at scale remain the most durable recipe for success.
At the platform level, Business-to-
Consumer Gross Order Value (B2C GOV) grew 45.5% year-on-year to INR 67 ,734 Crores, supported by 1.14 billion B2C orders, up 23.6%, and average Monthly Transacting Users (MTUs) of 23.5 million, up 33.1%. Consolidated Adjusted Revenue increased 48.9% to INR 24,315 Crores. More users engaged with multiple Swiggy services during the year, strengthening cross-pollination across the ecosystem and making the platform relevant across more everyday missions.
Equally important, the year 
strengthened our confidence in the operating architecture of the business. Food Delivery accelerated while improving profitability. Instamart scaled rapidly in a highly competitive category while making progress on unit economics. Out-of-Home Consumption delivered its first full year of profitability. Platform Innovations served as a structured space to test new propositions.
Food Delivery: Expanding the 
Category, Profitably
Food Delivery had a strong year, with 
GOV growing 20.2% to INR 34,593 Crores. Orders increased 13.6% to 714 million, while average MTUs grew 19 .2% to 17 .5 million. Average Order Value (AOV) moved from INR 458 to INR 484, reflecting a healthy balance of premiumisation and affordability-led propositions. Adjusted EBITDA crossed INR 1,000 Crores, up 76.7%, with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 2.9% of GOV. Contribution margin improved to 7 .5%, supported by advertising growth, better fleet utilisation and operating leverage.
The year also validated our view 
that Food Delivery has meaningful headroom in India. We built propositions across speed, selection, accessibility and value. Bolt and One BLCK addressed time-sensitive needs. 99 Store made the platform more accessible for value-conscious 
users. EatRight gained traction 
among consumers looking for healthier choices. DeskEats and Food on Train helped expand the platform into workplace and travel-linked occasions. These initiatives collectively created more reasons for consumers to use Swiggy and helped expand the addressable market.
The category can continue to 
expand if we keep solving sharper use cases and work with restaurant partners to improve affordability, reliability and choice.At the platform level, Business-
to-Consumer Gross Order Value (B2C GOV) grew 45.5% year-on-year to INR 67 ,734 Crores, supported by 1.14 billion B2C orders, up 23.6%, and average Monthly Transacting Users (MTUs) of 23.5 million, up 33.1%

Instamart: From Essentials to 
Everyday Convenience
Quick Commerce remained one of 
the most dynamic and competitive spaces in Indian retail. Instamart’s GOV grew 94.1% to INR 28,496 Crores, while Net Order Value (NOV) grew 69 .9% to INR 20,210 Crores. Orders increased 44.4% to 412 million. AOV rose from INR 514 to INR 691, supported by broader assortment, a higher non-grocery mix and larger-basket buying behaviour. Average MTUs grew 73.7% to 12.3 million.
Our strategy was not to pursue 
volume at any cost. We focussed on wallet share, basket quality, availability and operating leverage. Contribution margin improved to (2.8%) of GOV from (4.0%) in the previous year, led by higher AOVs, improved monetisation, better infrastructure utilisation and lower dependence on unsustainable incentives.
The Quick India Movement 
was an important milestone in communicating the new Instamart proposition. It helped users see Instamart not only as a grocery and essentials platform, but as a broader “everything store” across categories and occasions. 
We also took a more deliberate 
approach to network expansion. After front-loading investments in dark stores, our focus shifted towards sweating existing assets, improving utilisation and adding stores in a calibrated manner for coverage and debottlenecking. By year-end, Instamart had 1,143 active dark stores, up from 1,021, and total active dark store area of 4.8 million sq. ft. The infrastructure built can support significantly higher throughput as utilisation improves, alongside further assortment expansion for the primary addressable market.
The category will continue to attract 
capital and competition. Our answer is to build a business that wins through a distinctive product offering, dining remains underpenetrated even in top-tier cities, and we believe this segment can continue to grow as discretionary consumption expands.
Platform Innovations: Testing the 
Next Set of Use Cases
Platform Innovations exists as a 
deliberate sandbox for experiments that test new consumer propositions and business models. The idea is not to optimise only what exists, but to challenge existing paradigms where we see a large unmet need.
During the year, Toing was launched 
as an affordability-led experiment for budget-conscious consumers through a restaurant marketplace model. Crew was also introduced as part of our effort to explore newer convenience-led services. Not every experiment will scale at the same pace, but each helps us understand where our technology stack, fulfilment capability and consumer relationship can create future opportunities.
Capital Strength and the Ability 
to Execute
One of the key developments during 
the year was the strengthening of our balance sheet. We completed an INR 10,000 Crores Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), the second-largest ever in India outside the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector. The issue saw more than 4x demand from domestic and global investors, even amidst market volatility. Alongside the INR 2,400 Crores unlock from the Rapido stake sale, this gave us a much stronger capital base and a clear strategic advantage in highly competitive categories.
This matters because our categories 
are large, attractive and continue to evolve. It allows us to invest behind fulfilment infrastructure, technology, In 2022, Dineout was acquired as a high-engagement adjacency to Food Delivery, with the aim of building a stronger wrapper around restaurant experiences and creating additional revenue streams for the ecosystem. That thesis has played out well. Integration with the Swiggy app, cross-sell from Food Delivery, growth in restaurant partners, flagship dining events and increasing advertising monetisation have all contributed to the performance. In-restaurant product, brand, assortment and customer experience with a long-term orientation. It also gives us the confidence to make choices that are right for the business, even if they create temporary short-term trade-offs.
Responsible Growth
As Swiggy scales, we remain conscious that the platform is built on the strength of a large ecosystem. We remain focused on making our platform more inclusive and responsible. Whether it is strengthening social protection for delivery partners, through both internal welfare benefits and government initiatives like e-Shram; enabling more women to participate in the platform economy; supporting our restaurant and brand partners; or reducing the environmental footprint of our operations, we are committed to ensuring that growth is accompanied by meaningful progress. During the year, we continued to advance this agenda through consistent, measurable action. While there is more to do, our approach is clear: embed sustainability into the way we operate, innovate and grow.
Looking Ahead
The opportunity ahead remains large, and our focus is clear. We will continue to build for more users, more occasions and more purchase missions, while staying disciplined on capital allocation and operating choices. Our integrated platform, reusable technology stack, partner ecosystem and ability to move quickly give us a strong foundation to keep expanding the meaning of convenience for India’s urban consumers.
I would like to thank our shareholders not only through price. Quick delivery 
is increasingly becoming table stakes. The right to win will come from reliable availability, breadth of assortment, differentiated categories, strong partner brands and the ability to make Instamart a destination for everyday upgrades, not just everyday essentials. Early efforts such as Noice, our clean-food private brand, are part of this direction.
Out-of-Home Consumption:  
A Turnaround Story
Out-of-Home Consumption became 
one of the strongest turnaround stories in the portfolio. GOV grew 50.6% to INR 4,645 Crores, Adjusted Revenue increased 67 .3% to INR 412 Crores, and total transactions grew 58.4% to 15.1 million. The business delivered its first full year of profitability, with Adjusted EBITDA of INR 29 Crores and margin of 0.6% of GOV. Average monthly active restaurants grew 30.2% to 46.6k.for their continued trust and support. I also want to thank our users, delivery partners, restaurant partners, merchant and brand partners, employees and the Board for their trust, partnership and commitment to Swiggy’s journey.
We have always asked a simple 
question on behalf of the consumer: “Why not?” That question continues to guide us. It pushes us to reimagine convenience, build with urgency, learn with humility and execute with discipline.
Regards,Sriharsha Majety
Managing Director and  Group Chief Executive OfficerSwiggy Limited

Customer Proposition Highlights 
For Every Hunger, 
Habit and Household MissionDuring the year, we made Swiggy more relevant across 
everyday moments. A quick meal between meetings. A value-led order at the end of the month. A healthier lunch, an easier office food run, meals-on-the-train or a larger Instamart basket. We sharpened our platform around three customer promises: speed, value and choice. Each initiative created one more reason to open Swiggy and one more occasion to stay with us.

Bolt: Food That Keeps Pace With  
the Moment
Bolt took the idea of quick food delivery 
from a convenience feature to a mainstream behaviour. Live across 700+ cities and contributing over 1 in 10 food delivery orders, Bolt helped customers access fast-prep meals in minutes. It also strengthened Swiggy’s salience for impulse, in-between and time-sensitive food occasions.Express Delivery: Faster Access, Wider 
Availability 
Express Delivery was extended beyond Swiggy 
One BLCK, allowing more users to opt into faster delivery through an additional charge. This created a sharper speed-led choice for customers who want priority fulfilment, without limiting the experience to a premium subscription base.
Instamart: Speed With Broader Utility
Instamart continued to strengthen its promise of fast, reliable delivery while expanding what customers could buy. With larger stores, denser networks and megapods, speed became more than a grocery advantage. It became the foundation for quick commerce across many more missions.

When 
convenience must also feel worth it99 Store: Affordable Meals, 
Bigger Reach
99 Store scaled to 500+ cities, making 
everyday meals more accessible for price-conscious customers. Built around fast-prep, single-serve food, it helped Swiggy address a sharper affordability need without diluting the overall platform experience.
Maxxsaver: Making Larger Baskets 
Make Sense
Maxxsaver encouraged customers to build 
fuller Instamart carts by offering better value on larger baskets. This helped shift behaviour from top-up buying to more planned household purchases, improving both customer value and order economics.Quick India Movement: Value 
Meets Discovery
Quick India Movement gave Instamart a high-
energy sale format to showcase its expanded assortment. It helped customers discover that quick commerce could serve not just daily essentials, but also festive, seasonal, impulse and non-grocery purchase missions.
Swiggy One and Fee-Led Interventions: 
Reducing Friction
Through membership benefits, targeted 
affordability moves and sharper fee structures, we continued improving perceived value for customers. The focus was clear: make repeat usage easier, more rewarding and more relevant across services.

EatRight brought health-focussed curations such as High Protein, Low Calorie and No Added Sugar into everyday discovery. With 1 in 9 food delivery orders coming through these curations, it showed that healthier eating can scale when made visible, simple and accessible.
DeskEats: Solving the Office Food Mission
DeskEats expanded across 7 ,000+ tech parks in 30 cities, targeting one of the most repeatable food occasions: the workday meal. It made ordering at work easier, more affordable and better suited to weekday routines.Gourmet: Expanding Premium Food 
Discovery
While affordability widened access, Gourmet 
strengthened the premium end of the platform. By adding more curated restaurant options, it helped Swiggy serve higher-value occasions and balance everyday ordering with indulgent food experiences.
Food on Train: Convenience on the Move
Food on Train expanded to 115+ stations, extending Swiggy’s proposition beyond home, office and restaurant occasions. It brought better food access to travel moments where convenience has traditionally been limited.
Toing: Testing Food Delivery for Budget-
First Users
Launched during the year, Toing focuses on 
price-conscious customers such as students and early-jobbers. It allows us to test a different marketplace model for low-AOV meals, while continuing to expand affordability within the core app through 99 Store and Crazy Deals.
Crew: Extending Convenience into 
Everyday Assistance
Another platform innovation during the year was 
the launch of Crew, a personalised concierge-led offering for everyday assistance. From errands and bookings to planning support, it helps us test new ways to serve high-intent customer moments beyond ordering food, grocery or dining out.

Financial Profile
Sharper Economics. 
Stronger Foundation. 
Growth at Swiggy has never been about scale alone. As our 
platform expanded, FY 2025-26 was equally about building a business that grows stronger with scale. We sharpened operating discipline, improved monetisation across the ecosystem and strengthened our balance sheet to support long-term growth through evolving market cycles.
Scaling with Sharper Operating Discipline
Across the platform, we continued to improve 
structural profitability while investing behind growth opportunities and customer experience.
In Food Delivery, stronger operating leverage, 
rising advertising revenues and improved fleet utilisation supported margin expansion during the year. New propositions such as Bolt and 99 Store also gained meaningful traction by addressing distinct consumer needs around speed and affordability while supporting healthier delivery economics. 
In Quick Commerce, the focus remained on 
improving order quality, increasing wallet share and driving larger baskets instead of pursuing unsustainable discount-led growth. Megapods enabled deeper assortment expansion, while initiatives such as Maxxsaver supported larger carts, stronger wallet consolidation and improving contribution margins. The growing mix of non-grocery categories further strengthened engagement across use cases. Expanding Monetisation Beyond 
Transactions
As engagement across the platform deepened, 
we continued to strengthen monetisation beyond core transactions.
Advertising revenues scaled further across our 
ecosystem as more restaurant, merchant and brand partners leveraged the platform for visibility, discovery and customer acquisition. 
Swiggy One continued to strengthen retention 
and cross-platform engagement by improving affordability and convenience across food delivery, quick commerce and dining out. More than 35% of users were utilising multiple services on the platform by the end of the year, reflecting the growing strength of our integrated
 ecosy
stem.
Our integrated operating model also enabled us to unlock additional monetisation opportunities through adjacent offerings such as Dineout, Scenes and newer platform innovations, while leveraging a common technology stack, fulfilment network and user base across
 business
es.Strengthening the Balance Sheet for the 
Next Phase of Growth
During the year, we further strengthened our 
balance sheet, giving us the capital depth and flexibility to pursue long
-term growth.
We s
uccessfully completed an INR 10,000 Crores 
Qualified Institutional Placement, one of the largest non-BFSI QIPs in India. The issue saw strong participation from domestic and global institutional investors, reflecting confidence in our business fundamentals, execution capability and long-term opportunity.
Alongside this, the monetisation of our stake 
in Rapido unlocked approximately INR 2,400 Crores, further enhancing liquidity and financial flexibility.
Together, these actions have reinforced our 
ability to invest behind growth, innovation, infrastructure and customer propositions while maintaining disciplined fiscal prudence. In a dynamic and competitive hyperlocal commerce landscape, a stronger capital position gives us the confidence to execute consistently, stay agile and pursue our strategic priorities without making short-term trade-offs.
We also adopted a calibrated approach towards network expansion. Dark store additions increasingly prioritised utilisation, assortment depth and hyperlocal density rather than aggressive footprint growth alone. Our existing network today has the capacity to support more than 2x the current order base, enabling greater focus on sweating assets, improving utilisation and selectively expanding where required. 
Alongside this, we remained disciplined 
on user quality and long-term economics, with increasing emphasis on higher-value retained cohorts, wallet share and network productivity
 metrics.

Food Delivery
More Meals.  
More Moments.
FY2025-26 was a year of strong growth and improving profitability 
for Food Delivery, as we strengthened consumer engagement by unlocking newer consumption moments. 
The Year that Was
The business delivered strong momentum, with 
nearly 20% YoY GOV growth. We added 2.8  million 
MTUs during the year, while or
der growth improved 
to mid-teens from single digits in the previous year. 
Cross-pollination across the Swiggy ecosystem 
strengthened user growth, retention and frequency, with more consumers engaging across multiple services. Profitability also improved, with Contribution margins expanding to ~7 .5%, while Adjusted EBITDA crossed INR 1,000 Crores, nearly doubling from the previous year. Adjusted EBITDA margins reached ~2.9% of GOV, driven by advertising, better fleet utilisation and operating
 leverage
.
Built for Every Food Mission
Growth during the year was driven by propositions built around distinct consumer need states across speed, value, accessibility and premiumisation.
Bolt and One BLCK strengthened the speed-led 
proposition, with Bolt continuing to contribute more than 1 in 10 Food Delivery orders while opening up new consumption occasions across desserts, beverages, snacks and other fast-prep meals. Together, Bolt and 99 Store now account for around one-fifth of Food Delivery platform
 volumes.
The plat
form also expanded relevance across 
evolving food habits and routines. EatRight curations including High Protein, Low Calorie and No Added Sugar now contribute nearly 1 in 9 platform orders, reflecting rising demand for healthier food choices. DeskEats strengthened office food missions across tech parks in 30+ cities, while Food on Train expanded delivery access across railway-led travel occasions.At the premium end, Gourmet continued adding higher-value restaurant partners and balancing affordability-led growth with premiumisation-led AOV expansion.
Speed and Affordability
Affordability remained one of the biggest unlocks for category expansion during the year. However, the focus remained on building affordability sustainably rather than through structurally weak economics.
99 Store helped make ordering more accessible for 
value-conscious users while also driving higher-frequency behaviour. Propositions such as Bolt were designed around shorter delivery radii capabilities and fast-prep formats, helping optimise delivery economics while widening category participation.
Even as affordability initiatives expanded, overall 
user charges remained stable, while platform AOVs continued to stay healthy through premiumisation and broader consumption occasions. Swiggy One further strengthened user retention and repeat behaviour by deepening the connected membership ecosystem across Food Delivery, Quick Commerce and Dining Out.
Doing More with Every Order
Advertising continued emerging as an important profitability lever during the year, with restaurant partners increasingly adopting self-serve discovery and visibility tools on the platform.At the same time, improving fleet utilisation, stronger order density and operating leverage across fulfilment costs supported margin expansion even as the business continued investing behind newer propositions and affordability-led formats.
The combination of stronger user growth, 
rising monetisation and sharper operational efficiency continued strengthening the structural profitability profile of the business.
Miles to Go
Food Delivery in India is significantly underpenetrated relative to global markets, with meaningful headroom for higher frequency and broader adoption. As ordering habits expand beyond traditional meal occasions, we believe the next phase of growth will come from making Food Delivery more deeply embedded into everyday life across convenience-led, health-led, value-led and impulse consumption moments.

Quick Commerce
Bigger Baskets. 
Broader Missions.
Quick Commerce scaled rapidly while improving its economics, 
as Instamart strengthened its position from a fast grocery and essentials platform into an everyday convenience destination across categories and occasions.
The Year that Was
The business delivered strong GOV growth of 94.1% 
YoY to INR 28,496 Crores and NOV growth of 69 .9% YoY to INR 20,210 Crores, with Average Monthly Transacting Users rising 73.7% YoY to 12.3
 million. 
Average Or
der Value increased 34.4% YoY to INR 
691, driven by larger baskets and rising non-grocery adoption.
Profitability improved steadily despite heightened 
competition. Contribution margin improved to (2.8%) of GOV, while Adjusted EBITDA margin stood at (12.3%) of GOV, supported by better basket quality, improving dark store utilisation and operating leverage across fulfilment costs.
Beyond Grocery
Non-grocery categories emerged as a major growth driver during the year, with increasing traction across electronics, home and kitchen, toys, accessories, gifting and seasonal purchases. Instamart also strengthened its positioning as an “Everything Store” through Quick India Movement (QIM), the first large-format sale event by a quick commerce platform, designed to showcase class-leading selection beyond staples and essentials.
The platform’s assortment strategy remained a key 
differentiator, centred around hyperlocal selection, unique brand partnerships and expanding general merchandise offerings. Larger-format dark stores and megapods further strengthened category depth and fulfilment efficiency, while the platform maintained industry-leading speed across
 markets
.Building Larger Baskets
Basket expansion remained central to improving long-term platform economics and consumer engagement.
Maxxsaver continued scaling through its “cart-
within-a-cart” proposition, encouraging larger carts and stronger repeat behaviour. Alongside this, higher non-grocery adoption improved attach rates and helped consumers combine grocery, household and general merchandise purchases within the same order journey.
As a result, Average Order Value rose to INR
 691, 
while GOV gro
wth outpaced order growth, 
reflecting a stronger basket mix. The business 
remained focussed on driving the right kind of order growth through differentiated assortment, stronger consumer relevance and improving value, rather than pursuing structurally weak discount-led growth.
Scaling the Network
The dark store network continued expanding selectively, with a sharper focus on densification, throughput and assortment capability rather than footprint growth alone.
Instamart added 122 dark stores during the year 
to reach 1,143 stores across 125+ cities. Active dark store area increased to 4.8 million sq. ft., while average dark store size also increased as the business scaled larger-format stores and megapods to support broader assortment and higher throughput.
As the network matures, the focus remains 
on sweating existing assets while adding dark stores selectively for coverage and debottlenecking. The current infrastructure can support over 2X the current GOV, alongside further assortment expansion for the primary addressable market.
The integrated Swiggy ecosystem also 
strengthened user acquisition and retention, as more consumers engaged across Food Delivery, Quick Commerce and Dining Out through Swiggy One.
Only Getting Started
Quick Commerce in India remains at an early stage, with significant headroom across categories, frequency and wallet share. With industry-leading differentiated assortment, improving basket economics, reliable speed and a scalable network, Instamart remains well-positioned to capture the next phase of category growth as more shopping missions move to quick commerce.

Out-of-Home Consumption
Expanding Occasions 
Beyond the Home
Out-of-Home Consumption quietly became one of our 
strongest turnaround stories, delivering its first full year of profitability. The segment has evolved from an integrated acquisition into a high-growth platform that expands our role across the consumer’s food journey.The Year that Was
The business delivered strong GOV growth of 
50.6% YoY to INR 4,645 Crores, supported by rising consumer adoption, growing restaurant participation and a sharper dining-out proposition. Profitability improved through the year, with Adjusted EBITDA margin reaching 0.6% of GOV, supported by growing advertising revenue, low fulfilment costs, platform integration and operating leverage.
Dineout has been a success story since acquisition 
and broke even in early 2025, within two years of integration into the Swiggy app, reflecting the strength of our acquisition-led integration playbook.
Dineout at the Centre
Dineout remained the core of this segment, helping consumers discover restaurants, make reservations and complete payments through the Swiggy app. It has filled a clear whitespace in our hyperlocal portfolio and complemented our core Food Delivery business by extending our presence from ordering in to eating out.
For restaurants, it is increasingly becoming a strategic 
growth lever. Curated selections, social discovery, dining rewards and advertising solutions are helping partners improve visibility, drive footfall and encourage repeat visits.
Beyond Delivery
Dining out opens up a different food consumption opportunity, especially across premium restaurants, social occasions and higher discretionary spending.As of FY 2025-26, the segment had crossed 47k Average Monthly Active Restaurants, growing over 30% year-on-year. Many of these partners also operate on Food Delivery, creating a stronger discovery and retention flywheel across the Swiggy ecosystem. A meaningful share of new Dineout partners are premium dining restaurants, expanding access to a different food consumption opportunity and an incremental profit pool.
Experiences in the Making
Scenes remained nascent but added a new layer to our Out-of-Home proposition, allowing us to test curated events and hyperlocal experiences around dining, entertainment and social occasions. From live music to restaurant-led events, it brings discovery and booking into the same Swiggy journey, helping turn dining out into a fuller experience. As it evolves, Scenes gives us another way to deepen engagement, support restaurant partners and participate in more social occasions beyond the meal.
A Larger Seat at the Table
Dining out remains underpenetrated and has the potential to grow faster than Food Delivery over the medium term. With a growing partner base, premium dining expansion, inherently larger AOVs, low fulfilment costs and improving advertising monetisation, Dineout’s profitability is poised to strengthen further as the business
 scales
.

Enabling Zero-Emission Deliveries
EV adoption is central to our sustainability 
goals and we are building the infrastructure to make it accessible for our delivery partners and democratise access to green mobility. 
  Diverse Rental Choices: Delivery partners can choose fr
om over 60+ EV models during 
onboarding, enabling a transition to green mobility
  EV Giveaways & Incentives: To directly foster ownership
, and reward our fleet, we have 
launched targeted EV giveaway campaigns, placing zero-emission vehicles directly into the hands of our partners to accelerate EV adoption
Driven by these initiatives, our EV fleet has doubled since FY 2024-25, marking a massive 14x jump from our original baseline and successfully avoiding over 13,300 tCO
2e 
emissions in FY 2025 -26.
Thes
e initiatives form the core of our 
environmental impact strategy, leveraging technology to make every delivery count. Our Eco-Saver feature uses intelligent routing to optimise delivery paths, eliminating 8.9 million kilometres of travel and preventing 812.6 metric tonnes of CO
2e emissions in FY 2025-26 alone.
As a founding member of the UNEP Deliver-E Coalition, a global, industry-led alliance launched by major delivery platforms, Swiggy is spearheading the transition to sustainable last mile deliveries. We are aggressively driving the adoption of electric two wheelers across our
 operations.

Innovation

2

Strengthening Food Security & Safety and 
Enabling India’s Culinary Heritage
Swiggy leverages its platform architecture to make 
growth seamless for restaurant partners and enable food security. With hyperlocal discovery mechanisms, we actively promote India’s rich culinary legacy.
  In FY 2025-26 alone, we distributed 225,995 meals to underserved populations
. Operating in collaboration 
with Haldirams and the Robin Hood Army, this initiative deploys rapid redistribution logistics to channel refreshments to marginalised communities in Nagpur, Indore, and Raipur
  Leveraging our platform’s hyperlocal discovery mechanics, we pr
omote  India’s rich culinary 
heritage. By backing traditional and evolving food preferences, unique hyperlocal cuisines, such as Pahari, Bihari, and Goan, we are ensuring that regional culinary identities remain economically viable and vibrant
Building a Sustainable Digital Ecosystem 
Swiggy leverages technology as a primary enabler of eco-efficiency using platform architecture, and behavioral design to mitigate climate impact. By altering default choices, optimising digital infrastructure, and establishing marketplace incentives for sustainable materials, we drive circular economy principles across our entire commercial value
 chain:
  As part of our commitment to responsible tech stew
ardship, optimising our digital infrastructure 
and hosting our cloud services on AWS enabled us to avoid over 1,300 MtCO
2e in carbon emissions 
during FY 2025-26, yielding an environmental impact equivalent to the carbon absorbed by more than 21,000 trees growing for a decade
  Redesigning ordering environments can accelerate sustainable c
onsumer choices at scale. By 
implementing a “no cutlery” default for all food delivery orders, requiring users to actively opt in rather than opt out, we leveraged behavioral nudges to achieve more than 96% user adoption rate . This policy-aligned intervention drastically 
minimised single-use plastic waste and avoided 4,797 tonnes of CO
2e in FY 2025-26 alone, the 
ecological equivalent of planting a forest of 218,000 mature trees
  To facilitate sustainable packaging adoption among rest
aurant partners by 2030, we launched 
a dedicated Responsible Packaging Website. This digital B2B platform bridges the gap between environmental responsibility and commercial viability, generating over 2,600 partner leads. By securing exclusive 10-15% discounts from verified sustainable vendors on eco-friendly SKUs, our technology ensures that responsible choices are economically optimised for small and medium enterprises (SMEs)
Excellence in Corporate Governance
Swiggy maintains a multi-tiered ESG governance framework, with direct oversight from the Board-level Sustainability and CSR Committee, ensuring the strategic integration of environmental, social, and governance priorities. 
Furthermore, our robust risk management approach 
includes continuous identification and prioritisation of critical risks, such as Data Privacy and Cyber Security, and a comprehensive risk assessment for bribery and corruption conducted at least every three years. All identified risks are managed through documented mitigation and contingency plans.
We uphold a highly robust cybersecurity and privacy 
posture through a Unified Control Framework, integrating ISO 27001 (ISMS) and ISO 27701 (PIMS) certifications. This integrated governance satisfies stringent requirements like PCI-DSS and Data Localisation, ensuring customer data is secure, private, and stored within required geographic boundaries.

Average Order Value (AOV) Food Delivery GOV divided by Food Delivery Total Orders

Gross Revenue Revenue plus (i) user delivery charges collected and passed on to delivery partners (net of any discounts, including free delivery discounts provided through Swiggy One membership program), plus (ii) fee from users collected and netted off from platform funded discounts given for corresponding orders

Indian Economy
The Indian economy demonstrated strong resilience 
during FY 2025-26, reinforcing its position as one of the fastest-growing major economies globally despite geopolitical uncertainties and global economic moderation.  India’s real GDP is estimated at 7 .7% in  
FY 2025-26, according to the Second Advance Estimates, MoSPI, of gross domestic product (GDP) released by the government on February 27 , 2026, based on the new and updated series, highlighting the strength of domestic demand and structural reforms in driving economic expansion. Overall economic performance in FY 2025-26 was primarily due to robust real growth observed in Q2 (8.4%) and Q3 (7 .8%). 
Growth momentum during the fiscal year was supported by 
strong domestic consumption demand, rising infrastructure investment and expanding services activity across sectors such as finance, digital services and logistics. 
Inflationary pressures moderated significantly during the 
year, supported by easing food prices, improved supply conditions and policy measures aimed at maintaining macroeconomic stability. Average headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation for FY 2025-26 declined to 1.7%, while recent MoSPI data indicated 3.4% CPI inflation in March 2026, reflecting a moderation in food prices and improved supply conditions. The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), in its meeting held on April 8, 2026, projected CPI inflation at 4.6% for FY 2026-2 7.  
In response to the easing inflationary environment, the 
RBI’s MPC cumulatively reduced the repo rate by 100 basis points during its meetings from April to December 2025. As of December 2025, the repo rate stood at 5.25%. In its latest MPC meeting on April 8, 2026, the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged and maintained a neutral stance, reflecting the balancing act required amid evolving macroeconomic conditions, particularly geopolitical uncertainties and global supply chain disruptions.
Household consumption remained a key driver of India’s 
economic growth during FY 2025-26, supported by easing inflation, relatively stable employment conditions and improving real incomes. In addition, tax reforms and rationalisation measures contributed to stronger urban consumption and an improved spending environment. This supported growth in Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE), which increased by ~7% during  
FY 2025-26. According to the Economic Survey  
2025-26, PFCE accounted for nearly 61.5% of India’s GDP in  FY 2025-26, its highest share since 2012, underlining 
the importance of domestic consumption in sustaining economic growth.
As India enters FY 2026-27 , the global economic 
environment continues to face uncertainty arising from ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia, evolving trade restrictions and volatility in global commodity and energy markets. These developments have affected global supply chains, moderated investment sentiment and created uneven growth conditions across advanced and emerging economies. Despite these external challenges, India’s macroeconomic outlook remains relatively stable, supported by resilient domestic demand, policy continuity and improving economic fundamentals.
Following a year marked by structural policy measures and 
continued focus on economic formalisation, infrastructure development and manufacturing support, India enters FY 2026-27 with a relatively strong growth foundation. A diversified consumption base, sustained government capital expenditure, resilient services activity and continued support towards the manufacturing ecosystem are expected to support economic growth in the range of 6.8% to 7 .2% during FY 2026-27 , as projected in the Economic Survey 2025-26.

Annual Report 2025-26 Swiggy LimitedQuick Commerce Market
Quick commerce has emerged as one of the fastest-
growing segments within India’s retail landscape, supported 
by rising consumer preference for convenience, faster 
fulfilment and high-frequency digital purchasing behaviour. The market expanded significantly from approximately  
INR 4 billion (~USD 0.05 billion), representing nearly 0.01% of total retail in FY2020, to around INR 527 billion (~USD 
6.2 billion) and approximately 0.63% of total retail in  
FY2025. The market is projected to scale further to INR 4,505-6,025 billion (~USD 53-71 billion) by  
FY2030, accounting for nearly 4% of India’s retail market and 
implying a CAGR of 54-63% between FY2025 and FY2030. 
The rapid expansion of quick commerce is being driven 
by increasing consumer preference for faster fulfilment, predictable availability and seamless access across grocery, household essentials and an expanding range 
of discretionary categories. As speed, convenience and 
fulfilment reliability become increasingly central to urban consumption behaviour, quick commerce is evolving from a niche, impulse-led grocery format into a high-frequency, multi-category retail channel. Improvements in assortment 
depth, delivery density, routing efficiency and inventory management are further strengthening operating efficiency and enabling scale across hyperlocal delivery networks.
Within India’s online retail ecosystem, quick commerce has 
witnessed a sharp increase in market penetration, with its share rising from approximately 0.23% in FY2020 to around 8.86% in FY2025. The segment is projected to contribute nearly 30-33% of India’s online retail market by FY2030. 
This increasing penetration is supported by higher order 
frequency, rising consumer comfort with on-demand delivery models and continued expansion of assortments beyond grocery into categories such as beauty and personal care, home and kitchen products, small electronics and general merchandise. Improvements in delivery density, assortment management and service consistency continue to support faster growth relative to broader e-commerce and modern trade channels.
The pace of quick commerce adoption continues to vary 
across retail categories. Grocery, while remaining India’s largest retail category at approximately INR 51 trillion (~USD 
598 billion) in FY2025, continues to exhibit relatively low online and organised penetration. The category is projected to expand to approximately INR 73-81 trillion (~USD 855-
948 billion) by FY2030, with online penetration expected to increase to 6-7%, indicating significant headroom for digital adoption. In contrast, discretionary categories such as beauty and personal care, electronics and fashion show higher levels of formalisation and deeper online adoption, enabling a faster transition to on-demand fulfilment. As online penetration rises further across these categories, quick commerce is positioned to capture a growing share of category-level retail, with penetration expected to deepen across both essential and discretionary categories.

India’s digital economy, currently contributing about 13% of GDP, is projected to account for nearly 20% of India’s GDP by 2030, growing at almost twice the pace of the broader economy. Supported by 1.03 billion internet users, 660 million smartphones, and a digital payments ecosystem processing nearly 640 million UPI transactions daily, India is now the third-largest digitalised country in the world in terms of economy-wide digitalisation, according to the State of India’s Digital Economy Report 2025.
Digitally enabled industries have expanded significantly, 
with Information and Communication Technology (ICT) services and the manufacturing of electronic components, computers and communication equipment contributing 7 .83% of gross value added (GVA), while digital platforms and intermediaries contributed another 2% of GVA. In addition, digital adoption across sectors such as BFSI, retail and education added a further 2% to GVA, reflecting the increasing integration of digital technologies across the economy. The digital economy’s share is projected to rise to nearly 20% of GVA by 2030.
India’s Retail Market
India’s retail market continued to expand steadily, driven by rising household consumption, increasing discretionary spending and deeper digital penetration across urban and emerging markets. The retail market 
grew from approximately INR 62 trillion (~USD 725 billion) in  
FY 2020 to around INR 83 trillion (~USD 978 billion) in  
FY 2025, registering a CAGR of nearly 6% during the period. The market is projected to expand further to  
INR 123-135 trillion (~USD 1.4-1.6 trillion) by FY 2030, 
implying a CAGR of 8-10% between FY 2025 and  
FY 2030.
Grocery remained the largest category within India’s 
retail market, accounting for nearly 61% of total retail consumption in FY 2025, and is projected to contribute around 59% by FY 2030, reflecting its essential and high-frequency consumption nature. At the same time, non-grocery categories are expected to witness faster growth, supported by rising affluence, broader product accessibility and increasing digital adoption across city tiers. Non-grocery segments are projected to grow at a CAGR of 9–11% between FY 2025 and FY 2030, increasing their share of the retail market from around 39% in FY 2025 to nearly 41% by FY 2030. Categories such as fashion, electronics, beauty and personal care are expected to benefit from rising consumer preference for variety, convenience, faster fulfilment and improved digital access, supporting the continued evolution of India’s hyperlocal and on-demand consumption ecosystem.

Annual Report 2025-26• Hyperlocal Operating Model and Netw ork Efficiency
  Quick commerc
e operates on a hyperlocal fulfilment 
architecture, where delivery performance and 
operating efficiency are driven by city-level and micro-market optimisation. Increasing dark-store density, calibrated assortment planning and routing efficiencies are improving fulfilment reliability and supporting better asset utilisation. Platforms are also optimising product mix towards higher-margin and higher-AOV categories, supporting gradual improvement in contribution margins as networks scale. The operating model continues to evolve between inventory-led and marketplace-led structures, balancing assortment control, service consistency and working capital intensity.
•
 Emerging Advert
ising and Discovery Ecosystem
  Quick commerce plat
forms are increasingly evolving 
into high-intent discovery and advertising channels for consumer brands. With users engaging across multiple purchase occasions and categories, these platforms provide brands with contextual visibility close to the point of transaction. Online retail platforms accounted for approximately 18% of India’s digital advertising market in FY 2025. Advertising monetisation within quick commerce is also gaining scale, with advertising revenues already contributing around 4-5% of GMV for certain platforms during FY 2025. Improvements in targeting capabilities using location, purchase behaviour and category affinity are enabling stronger campaign effectiveness, with Return on Advertising Spend (RoAS) reaching nearly 5-8x in certain use cases.•
  Increasing Contribution from Non-Grocery Categories
  Quick commerce is s
teadily expanding beyond 
grocery into discretionary categories such as beauty and personal care, electronics, fashion, home and kitchen products and general merchandise. Adoption across non-grocery categories is projected to grow 1.4-1.6x faster between FY2025 and FY2030,  
supported by rising consumer preference for convenience-led purchases and faster fulfilment across everyday discretionary needs. This shift is reflected in the increasing contribution of non-grocery categories to quick commerce Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), with their share projected to increase from approximately 23% in FY2025 to 36-40% by FY2030.
Indian Food Service Market
India’s food services market accounted for approximately 13% of India’s total food consumption market in FY 2025, compared with nearly 11% in FY2020, and is projected to increase to 15–16% by FY2030. The market continues to expand steadily, supported by increasing out-of-home consumption, rising participation of organised formats and wider digital adoption across ordering-in and dining-out occasions.
In value terms, the market grew from approximately  
INR 4 trillion (~USD 52 billion) in FY2020 to nearly INR 7 trillion 
 (~USD 79 billion) in FY2025 and is projected to reach INR 
11-12 trillion (~USD 135-140 billion) by FY2030, implying a CAGR of 11-12% between FY2025 and FY2030. Growth is being supported by changing urban lifestyles, rising disposable incomes, smaller household structures and increasing consumer preference for convenience-led food consumption. • Habit-led Consumption Behaviour
  India’s consumption lands
cape is characterised by 
frequent, smaller-ticket purchases across grocery, 
fresh produce and household essentials. Quick commerce aligns closely with these consumption patterns by enabling rapid fulfilment and reliable access for immediate-use requirements. As delivery consistency and service reliability improve, consumers are increasingly integrating quick commerce into routine purchasing behaviour rather than using it only for urgent or impulse-led needs. This behavioural shift is contributing to higher order frequency, improving basket sizes and rising Average Order Values (AOVs) across platforms.•
 Expansion across Tier 1 and Tier 2+ Cit
ies
  The continued expansion of dark -store infrastructure 
across metro along with deeper penetration into Tier 1 and Tier 2+ cities, is improving reach, delivery speed and service consistency for quick commerce channels. While metro markets continue to benefit from higher order density and mature consumer adoption, Tier 1 and Tier 2+ cities are witnessing faster growth driven by rising disposable incomes, increasing digital familiarity and greater adoption of app-based commerce models. Quick commerce is well-positioned to scale in these markets, with the quick commerce market in Tier 1 and Tier 2+ cities projected to grow at a CAGR of 76-88% between FY 2025 and

India’s online food delivery market is witnessing higher user engagement as food delivery increasingly becomes part of routine consumption behaviour. Annual Transacting Users (ATUs) increased from 50-60 million in FY 2020 to 90-105 million in FY 2025 and are projected to reach 145-170 million by FY 2030. Monthly Transacting Users (MTUs) increased from 12-18 million in FY 2020 to 25-35 million in FY 2025 and are expected to increase further to 44-65 million by FY 2030, reflecting stronger platform engagement and improving ordering frequency.
Increasing preference for convenience, speed and 
wider food choices is supporting growth in online food delivery across urban markets. Demand is also expanding beyond indulgence-led occasions towards routine meal consumption, supported by greater availability of value offerings, specialised cuisines and healthier food options.
Platforms continue to improve fulfilment efficiency through 
denser delivery networks, enhanced rider allocation and technology-led route optimisation. Faster delivery timelines and higher service reliability are contributing to improved customer retention and repeat ordering behaviour.
Online food delivery platforms are increasingly catering 
to multiple consumption occasions, including meals, snacks, breakfast and single-serve requirements. Wider menu assortment, combo offerings and value packs are supporting higher order frequency and expanding the addressable consumer base.
Improved app interfaces, personalised recommendations 
and loyalty programmes are strengthening customer engagement across platforms. Technology-led menu discovery, restaurant recommendations and logistics optimisation are also improving user experience and supporting higher repeat consumption.Rising Ordering

Annual Report 2025-26 Swiggy LimitedSwiggy’s Out-of-Home consumption segment has two primary services, Swiggy 
Dineout and Swiggy Scenes. Dineout offers a platform for users to discover 
restaurants and make reservations, while Scenes is a dedicated platform for booking in-restaurant events, enhancing the Company’s presence in dining-related services beyond food delivery. The services leverage Swiggy’s consumer base and tech capabilities, cross-pollinating users and brand salience for a stronger relationship with both users and restaurant partners. Dineout was one of the few acquisitions by Swiggy in its journey and was integrated into its unified app a couple of years back. These services strengthen Swiggy’s presence in the lifestyle and dining space, catering to the evolving preferences of urban consumers seeking premium dining and entertainment options. 
In FY 2025-26, the Out-of-Home Consumption segment continued to scale and 
move towards profitability, with GOV increasing by 50.6% YoY to INR 4,645 Crores, while Monthly Active Restaurants increased by 30.2% to approximately 47k.Out-of-Home 
Consumption 
As a technology-led platform, Swiggy continues to build, test and scale new 
offerings aligned with its focus on convenience-led consumption. These include adjacent businesses as well as emerging platform opportunities across hyperlocal commerce and digital services. Recent initiatives include Toing, an experimental marketplace designed to explore affordable food delivery and expand category penetration among value-conscious consumers. Swiggy also introduced Crew, a concierge-style assistance platform that helps users plan, coordinate and simplify everyday tasks and experiences, extending convenience beyond transactions.Platform

The business offers integrated warehousing services, including inventory management, in-warehouse processing and packaging solutions, alongside distribution capabilities supported by Swiggy’s logistics network. Swiggy Networks (Scootsy) also partners with brands to support retail expansion and improve distribution reach across markets. By leveraging technology-enabled fulfilment and logistics capabilities, the business aims to improve operational efficiency and delivery reliability across the supply chain ecosystem.Supply Chain and 
Distribution Company Overview
Swiggy Limited (hereafter referred to as “Swiggy” or “the 
Company”) is India’s pioneering on-demand convenience platform, transforming the way consumers access food and everyday essentials. Swiggy offers a range of user-friendly services that enable customers to browse, select, order and pay for food, groceries and household essentials, with deliveries fulfilled through its on-demand delivery partner network.
Established in 2013, the Company was founded with a 
mission to enhance the quality of life for urban consumers by providing seamless access to daily essentials. Over the years, Swiggy has emerged as a leading player in India’s online food delivery market by leveraging robust technology capabilities, an extensive delivery network and a customer-centric operating model.Swiggy has progressively diversified its offerings beyond 
food delivery to include Swiggy Instamart, its quick commerce platform for groceries and household essentials, and Swiggy Dineout, which offers restaurant discovery, table reservations and dining-related experiences. The platform partners with hundreds of thousands of restaurants, retail merchants, brand partners and delivery executives across hundreds of cities, with a focus on enabling reliable and convenient hyperlocal commerce experiences.
Backed by leading global and domestic investors, Swiggy 
continues to focus on innovation, operational efficiency and customer experience across its platform ecosystem. The Company remains focussed on strengthening its position within India’s rapidly evolving digital consumption and hyperlocal delivery landscape.
Swiggy’s Food Delivery business remains the cornerstone of its platform ecosystem, 
offering a comprehensive on-demand food delivery service that connects customers with a wide selection of restaurant partners through its app and website. The overall platform service currently operates across 720+ cities in India and caters to approximately 18.3 million Monthly Transacting Users (MTUs). In addition to order fulfilment, the platform also provides advertising and visibility solutions to restaurant partners, supporting customer discovery and engagement across the network.  
In FY 2025-26, the Food Delivery segment delivered steady growth, with Gross 
Order Value (GOV) increasing by 20.2% year-on-year (YoY) to INR 34,593 Crores, while MTUs increased by 19 .2% to 17 .5 million. 
Swiggy’s Quick Commerce business, Instamart, focuses on rapid delivery of groceries 
and household essentials through a dense hyperlocal fulfilment network. Since its launch in 2020, Instamart has expanded its presence to 125+ cities, supported by a network of 1,143 active dark stores across India. Backed by dedicated delivery infrastructure, the platform has reduced delivery timelines to approximately  
13 minutes.
Over time, the business has expanded beyond grocery-led use cases to include 
a wider assortment across non-grocery categories, resulting in larger dark-store formats and broader SKU availability. Instamart has also introduced larger-format dark stores, referred to as “megapods”, spanning approximately  
8-10k sq. ft., capable of housing up to 50k SKUs.
In FY 2025-26, the Quick Commerce segment witnessed strong scale-up, with 
GOV increasing by 94.1% YoY to INR 28,496 Crores and MTUs rising by 73.7% to 12.3 million. Average Order Value (AOV) increased by 34.4% YoY to INR 691, supported by broader assortment availability and increasing consumer adoption. During the year, the Company added 122 stores, resulting in a significant increase in active dark-store area to approximately 4.8 million sq. ft., representing growth of 21.1% YoY.  Food Delivery
Quick CommerceDiversified Offerings

Annual Report 2025-26 Swiggy LimitedTechnology and Information Security 
Governance
Reliable, secure and scalable technology is fundamental to 
our operations. System interruptions or capacity constraints could affect availability and the customer experience, while an evolving threat landscape exposes us to cyber incidents such as social engineering, denial-of-service attacks, credential-based attacks, and malware. A significant incident could disrupt services, affect data, and carry financial and reputational risks.
We operate dedicated security teams and defined 
frameworks, supported by advanced security tooling, regular testing & maintenance, resilience, and business continuity planning. We run bug-bounty programmes and internal initiatives such as hackathons to identify and address vulnerabilities, conduct periodic security assessments, and sustain a strong security culture through ongoing employee awareness and training.
Data Privacy and Responsible AI
Governance
As a platform that processes personal data at scale, we are 
responsible for protecting the data and for complying with an evolving data-protection and privacy regime, including India’s data-protection law. A shortfall in safeguarding personal data or in meeting applicable obligations could lead to regulatory, financial and trust-related  
consequences.
We are also expanding our use of artificial intelligence 
across several business operations. While these technologies create meaningful opportunities to improve experience and efficiency, they also introduce considerations relating to the accuracy and reliability of outputs, fairness, transparency, the responsible use of data, dependence on third-party models, and a developing regulatory landscape. The same technologies can also be used by external parties to increase the sophistication of cyber and fraud-related activity, which we factor into our defences.
We follow privacy-by-design principles, supported by 
data governance and privacy protocols, so that personal data is processed lawfully, securely, and transparently, and we continue to align our practices with applicable  
requirements. For artificial intelligence, we are strengthening governance for responsible development and use —  
including appropriate human oversight, review of model performance and outcomes, and controls over data and third-party tools — so that these technologies are deployed safely, ethically and consistently with our values and obligations.Regulatory and Compliance Landscape 
Governance
We operate across food delivery, quick commerce and 
adjacent services in a dynamic regulatory environment. Changes in laws and regulations, or in their interpretation and enforcement — including those relating to our business model, social security of gig workers, food safety and quality standards, data protection, foreign investment and permitted business models, consumer protection, competition and taxation — could increase our cost of compliance, require adjustments to our business practices, or give rise to claims and operational restrictions.
We maintain a compliance framework and monitor regulatory 
developments on an ongoing basis. Our legal, compliance and secretarial functions, supported by external advisors where appropriate, work to ensure timely alignment with applicable requirements, and regulatory considerations are embedded within our planning and operational decisions.
Macroeconomic and Geopolitical Environment
Social & Governance 
Our performance is influenced by broader macroeconomic 
and geopolitical conditions, including movements in inflation, interest rates, and currencies, as well as shifts in consumer sentiment and discretionary spending. A slowdown in consumption or wider economic or geopolitical uncertainty could moderate demand, affect order frequency and values, and increase operating costs.
Our diversified portfolio across food delivery, quick 
commerce, and adjacent services — spanning a range of customer needs, price points, and use cases, including everyday essentials — helps moderate the effects of economic cycles. We monitor macroeconomic and market trends on an ongoing basis and adapt our product, pricing, and resource allocation decisions accordingly, with a continued emphasis on efficiency and resilience.
Talent and Organisation 
Social 
Our ability to attract, develop, and retain talented people, 
together with the strength of our leadership pipeline and succession planning, is important to our ability to grow, innovate, and develop technologically. Difficulty in securing or retaining critical skills could affect our execution and competitiveness.
We invest in our people through structured learning, 
leadership development, and career growth opportunities, including capability building in emerging areas. We support well-being through flexible policies and wellness initiatives, foster an inclusive and diverse workplace underpinned by fair and transparent performance practices, and listen to our people through regular feedback mechanisms to strengthen engagement and retention.Risk Management 
Swiggy recognises that risk management is integral to the Company’s strategy. We believe our success as an organisation depends on our ability to identify and leverage opportunities while managing the risks that accompany them. The board has constituted a Risk Management Committee responsible for overseeing the Company’s risk management framework, reviewing the Company’s risk profile periodically, and ensuring that adequate processes are in place for the identification, assessment, and mitigation of key risks.
Our enterprise risk management framework is embedded 
within strategic and operational decision-making. Risks are identified at both the Company and individual business levels, assessed on the basis of their potential impact and likelihood, assigned clear ownership, and the effectiveness of mitigation plans is monitored. Governance of risk is organised in line with the Three Lines Model, all of which are under the oversight of the Board and its Committees.
The Enterprise Risk Management team drives risk-
management procedures across the organisation, and the framework is reviewed periodically to keep pace with emerging risks and developments in our markets and industry. The policy was last revised in October, 2025 in line with SEBI Listing Regulations. The Updated Risk Management Policy can be accessed at https://www.swiggy.com/corporate/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Swiggy-RMC-Policy-ERM.pdf.
Each principal risk set out below is mapped to the sustainability dimension it most closely relates to — Environmental (E), Social (S) or Governance (G) — and is described together with the way we seek to manage it.
Service Quality and Customer Trust
Governance
Swiggy’s growth rests on consumer trust and the strength 
of its network of restaurants, delivery partners, sellers, and brand partners. Inconsistent service quality, delays or availability interruptions, errors in fulfilment, or an inconsistent support experience could weaken confidence, reduce engagement, and affect retention across our food delivery, quick commerce, and other offerings.
We invest continuously in product innovation, service 
reliability and responsive support, including specialised resolution channels and structured training for our consumer- and partner-facing teams. Feedback from consumers and partners is tracked closely and channelled back into product and operational improvements, and we monitor service and satisfaction indicators across each business to sustain a consistent, high-quality experience.Brand and Reputation
Governance
The strength of the Swiggy brand is central to user 
acquisition, partner participation and long-term value creation. Commentary or publicity concerning our business model, partner earnings and well-being, technology, privacy, sustainability practices, or financial performance, as well as intellectual property matters, can influence how the brand is perceived and may give rise to remediation costs.
We maintain clear brand and communication guidelines 
and a dedicated function that monitors public sentiment and responds in a timely and transparent manner. We proactively share the Company’s progress and contributions with stakeholders and communities, while a consumer-insights function engages with stakeholders to inform continuous improvement of our products and services.
Competition
Governance
We operate in highly competitive and rapidly evolving 
markets. Existing and new competitors may introduce differentiated products, alternative pricing or business models, or invest significantly in promotions and capacity, particularly in the quick commerce segment. Such competition could affect our market position, growth and profitability.
We compete through continuous innovation, a deep 
understanding of consumer behaviour, and a sustained focus on the experience we offer consumers and partners. We strengthen our position through differentiated products, efficient operations, disciplined investment, and the breadth of our portfolio spanning food delivery, quick commerce, and adjacent services.
Ecosystem and Stakeholder Dependence | Social & 
Governance 
Our operations rely on a large ecosystem of delivery 
partners, restaurant and seller partners, and third-party providers (i.e. technology, payments, etc.). The availability, engagement and well-being of delivery partners, continuity of supply from partners and the dependability of key third parties are important to service continuity. In addition, the evolving regulatory framework for gig workers may over time influence our operating costs and compliance requirements.
We work closely with each stakeholder group through 
dedicated support teams, timely grievance resolution, and regular training on service quality, safety and responsible practices. We extend well-being measures to delivery partners, including insurance cover and health and safety initiatives, and we forecast capacity requirements to secure availability and continuity of service. We continue to monitor developments in the regulation of gig workers and engage constructively to adapt our practices accordingly.

Annual Report 2025-26Human Resources
Swiggy considers its people central to its long-term growth 
and continues to foster a high-performance, inclusive and collaborative workplace culture. The Company focuses on building organisational capability through structured learning programmes, leadership development initiatives and career progression opportunities, while also supporting employee well-being through flexible work practices and wellness initiatives.

The Company has established adequate internal control systems, supported by a comprehensive internal audit framework. These controls are designed to ensure the accuracy and reliability of financial reporting, safeguard assets and maintain appropriate operational and financial accountability. During FY 2025-26, the effectiveness of these controls was reviewed, and no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies were identified.
